pumac-2024-algebra-a-07.title: A telescoping identity for the angles
pumac-2024-algebra-a-07.body:
Let $\theta_n=\arctan\frac1{F_n}$. For even $n$, Cassini/d'Ocagne gives $F_nF_{n+1}+1=F_{n-1}F_{n+2}$, so
$$\tan(\theta_n-\theta_{n+1})=\frac{F_{n+1}-F_n}{F_nF_{n+1}+1}=\frac{F_{n-1}}{F_{n-1}F_{n+2}}=\frac1{F_{n+2}},$$
i.e. $\theta_{n}=\theta_{n+1}+\theta_{n+2}$ for even $n$ (the hint is $n=2$). Also $\theta_1=\theta_2=\frac\pi4$.

Put $x_k=\theta_{2k}$ and $y_k=\theta_{2k+1}$. Then $y_k=x_k-x_{k+1}$, and $x_k\to0$. Split $S$ into the first term and pairs:
$$S=\theta_1\theta_2+\sum_{k\ge1}\big(\theta_{2k}\theta_{2k+1}+\theta_{2k+1}\theta_{2k+2}\big)=x_1^2+\sum_{k\ge1}y_k(x_k+x_{k+1}).$$
Now $y_k(x_k+x_{k+1})=(x_k-x_{k+1})(x_k+x_{k+1})=x_k^2-x_{k+1}^2$, which telescopes to $x_1^2$. Thus
$$S=2x_1^2=2\cdot\frac{\pi^2}{16}=\frac{\pi^2}8,$$
and $80S=10\pi^2\approx98.70$, so $\lfloor80S\rfloor=98$.

**Answer: 98**

pumac-2024-algebra-a-07.title: Numerical confirmation
pumac-2024-algebra-a-07.body:
Summing the first 150 terms numerically gives $S=1.2337005501\ldots=\pi^2/8$, so $80S\approx98.696$.

**Answer: 98**

pumac-2024-algebra-a-08.title: Cyclotomic polynomial and resultants
pumac-2024-algebra-a-08.body:
Write $n=2024=2^3\cdot11\cdot23$. The primitive $n$th roots are the $\omega_n^i$ with $\gcd(i,n)=1$, so $\prod_i(x-\omega_n^i)=\Phi_n(x)$. As $\varphi(n)$ is even,
$$f(n)=\prod_{\gcd(j,n)\ne1}\Phi_n(\omega_n^j)\quad(\text{up to sign}).$$
The roots $\omega_n^j$ with $\gcd(j,n)\ne1$ are the primitive $d$th roots of unity for the divisors $d\mid n$, $d<n$; each $d$ occurs $\varphi(d)$ times. So $|f(n)|=\prod_{d\mid n,\,d<n}|\mathrm{Res}(\Phi_d,\Phi_n)|$.

Use the classical fact: for $d<n$, $d\mid n$,
$$\mathrm{Res}(\Phi_d,\Phi_n)=\begin{cases}p^{\varphi(d)}&\text{if } n/d=p^k \text{ is a prime power},\\ 1&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
For $n=2024$ the divisors $d$ with $n/d$ a prime power are:
- $n/d=2,4,8$: $d=1012,506,253$ with $\varphi=440,220,220$, contributing $2^{880}$;
- $n/d=11$: $d=184$, $\varphi(184)=88$, contributing $11^{88}$;
- $n/d=23$: $d=88$, $\varphi(88)=40$, contributing $23^{40}$.

So $e_1=880$, $e_2=88$, $e_3=40$ and $e_1+e_2+e_3=1008$.

**Answer: 1008**

pumac-2024-algebra-a-08.title: Checking the formula on small $n$
pumac-2024-algebra-a-08.body:
The same computation for $n=12,18,30$ gives $f=2^4 3^2,\ 2^6 3^3,\ 2^8 3^4 5^2$, which agrees with direct numerical evaluation of the double product ($144,\ 1728,\ 518400$). Applying it to $2024$ gives the exponents above.

**Answer: 1008**
